## Table of Laplace Transforms

We can choose a *laplace transform* to a given function based on the following table. Assume $a$ and $c$ are a constants.

\

```{=latex}
\begin{center}
{\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{2.5}
\begin{tabular}{|l|l|}
\hline
$\displaystyle f(t) = \mathcal{L}^{-1}\{F(s)\}$                & $\displaystyle F(s) = \mathcal{L}\{f(t)\}$ \\ \hline
$\displaystyle 1$                                              & $\displaystyle \frac{1}{s}$                \\ \hline
$\displaystyle e^{a \ t}$                                      & $\displaystyle \frac{1}{s-a}$              \\ \hline
$\displaystyle t^n, \ n=1,2,\cdots$                            & $\displaystyle \frac{n!}{s^{n+1}}$         \\ \hline
$\displaystyle \sin{(a \ t)}$                                   & $\displaystyle \frac{a}{s^2 + a^2}$        \\ \hline
$\displaystyle \cos{(a \ t)}$                                   & $\displaystyle \frac{s}{s^2 + a^2}$        \\ \hline
$\displaystyle \sinh{(a \ t)}$                                  & $\displaystyle \frac{a}{s^2 - a^2}$        \\ \hline
$\displaystyle \cosh{(a \ t)}$                                  & $\displaystyle \frac{s}{s^2 - a^2}$        \\ \hline
heavyside function $\displaystyle \rightarrow u_c (t) = u(t-c)$  & $\displaystyle \frac{e^{-c \ s}}{s}$       \\ \hline
dirac delta function $\displaystyle \rightarrow \delta(t - c)$ & $\displaystyle e^{-c \ s}$                 \\ \hline
 1st derivative $\displaystyle \rightarrow f'(t)$                                          & $\displaystyle sF(s) - f(0)$               \\ \hline
2nd derivative $\displaystyle \rightarrow f''(t)$                                          & $\displaystyle s^2 F(s) - sf(0) - f'(0)$   \\ \hline
\end{tabular}
}
\end{center}
```

\

*Note: This list only contains some of the more commonly used laplace transforms and formulas.*
